# Dhammadevaputtajātaka (Ja 457)

**ID:** Ja 457
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Dhammadevaputtajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Deity Named Dhamma

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammadevaputtajātaka* (Ja 457), also referred to as the *Dhamma Jātaka*, is a canonical birth story set at Jetavana [SuttaCentral; Boriharnwanaket]. The narrative occasion arises when monks discuss Devadatta being swallowed by the earth on account of his enmity with the Tathāgata. The Buddha relates that in a previous existence Devadatta had likewise struck against the authority of righteousness, leading to him being swallowed into the nethermost hell [SuttaCentral]. In that past life, the Bodhisatta appeared as the deity Dhamma (Dhammadevaputta) and contended with Adhamma (Devadatta's former birth) [SuttaCentral; Levman 2014; Boriharnwanaket]. The text features a verse debate between Right and Wrong, and contains the phrase *vāmam karoti* describing Adhamma making an adverse "leftwards circuit" around Jambudvīpa [Levman 2014; Boriharnwanaket]. In exegetical tradition, the Bodhisatta's birth as Dhammadevaputta is cited in the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* as an illustration of the perfection of patience (*adhivāsanakkhanti*) [Endo 1997].

The text is referenced elsewhere in later Pali literature in the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.4.7) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse data computed by DharmaNexus shows extensive Pali-internal sharing with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (volume 4, particularly §2.1–8.1) and the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§1.1–7.4), in which parallel stanzas are quoted and compared [DharmaNexus; Boriharnwanaket]. DharmaNexus also records machine alignments with Tibetan and Chinese corpora, including the *Upāyakauśalya-sūtra* (D0261), the *Qishi yinben jing* (T 25), the *Qishi jing* (T 24), and the *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
